'''Anna Igorevna Krylov''' (Russian: Анна Игоревна Крылова) is the USC Associates Chair in Natural Sciences and Professor of [[Chemistry]] at the [[University of Southern California]] (USC). Working in the field of theoretical and computational [[quantum chemistry]], she is the inventor of the spin-flip method.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lischka|first1=Hans|last2=Nachtigallová|first2=Dana|last3=Aquino|first3=Adélia J. A.|last4=Szalay|first4=Péter G.|last5=Plasser|first5=Felix|last6=Machado|first6=Francisco B. C.|last7=Barbatti|first7=Mario|date=2018-08-08|title=Multireference Approaches for Excited States of Molecules|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.chemrev.8b00244|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=118|issue=15|pages=7293–7361|doi=10.1021/acs.chemrev.8b00244|pmid=30040389|s2cid=206542530 |issn=0009-2665}}</ref> Krylov has received worldwide recognition, in particular for her invention of the spin-flip method, has served on the editorial boards of numerous peer-review journals, and is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], the [[American Chemical Society]], the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. She is the president of [[Q-Chem#History|Q-Chem, Inc.]]<ref name=":0" /> and an elected member of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]], the [[Academia Europaea]], the American Academy of Sciences and Letters,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anna I. Krylov |url=https://academysciencesletters.org/member/anna-i-krylov/ |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=American Academy of Sciences & Letters |language=en-US}}</ref> and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].

== Life and education ==
Born in [[Donetsk]], Ukraine, Krylov received her [[M.Sc.]] ([[Honours degree|with honors]]) in [[Chemistry]] from [[Moscow State University]] in 1990 and her [[Ph.D.]] (''[[summa cum laude]]'') from [[The Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] working under the supervision of Professor [[Robert Benny Gerber]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Faculty Profile > USC Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences|url=http://dornsifelive.usc.edu/wrapper/cf/faculty-and-staff/faculty.cfm|access-date=2021-03-14|website=dornsifelive.usc.edu|language=en}}</ref> Her Ph.D. research at the Fritz Haber Center for Molecular Dynamics<ref>{{cite web |title=Fritz Haber Center for Molecular Dynamics |url=https://fhrc.huji.ac.il/ |website=fhrc.huji.ac.il |publisher=Hebrew University / the Minerva Foundation Fritz Haber Center for Molecular Dynamics |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref> focused on molecular dynamics in rare gas clusters and matrices.

== Career ==
Upon completing her Ph.D. in 1996, Krylov joined the group of Prof. [[Martin Head-Gordon]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], as a [[postdoctoral research]] associate, where she became involved with electronic structure method development. In 1998, she joined the Department of Chemistry at [[University of Southern California|USC]].

=== Research ===
Professor Krylov leads the iOpenShell lab,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://iopenshell.usc.edu|title=Laboratory for Theoretical Studies of Electronic Structure and Spectroscopy of Open-Shell and Electronically Excited Species - iOpenShell|website=iopenshell.USC.edu|access-date=2 January 2018}}</ref> a research group focused on theoretical modeling of [[open shell|open-shell]] and electronically excited species.  She develops robust black-box methods to describe complicated multi-configurational wave functions in single-reference formalisms, such as coupled-cluster and equation-of-motion (or linear response) approaches. She developed the spin-flip approach,<ref name="auto">Size-consistent wave functions for bond-breaking: The equation-of-motion spin-flip model Chem. Phys. Lett., 338, 375–384 (2001)</ref><ref name="auto1">The spin-flip equation-of-motion coupled-cluster electronic structure method for a description of excited states, bond-breaking, diradicals, and triradicals Acc. Chem. Res., 39, 83–91 (2006)</ref> which extends coupled-cluster and [[Density functional theory|density functional]] methods to biradicals, triradicals, and bond-breaking. Krylov has also contributed to the development of molecular orbital concepts in the framework of many-body wave functions and to the extension of molecular orbital theory to the domain of non-linear optical properties and meta-stable electronic states.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Krylov|first=Anna I.|date=2020-08-24|title=From orbitals to observables and back|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=153|issue=8|pages=080901|doi=10.1063/5.0018597|pmid=32872858 |issn=0021-9606|doi-access=free}}</ref> In addition, Krylov develops [[Many-body problem|many-body]] theories for describing [[metastable]] electronic states (resonances) and tools for spectroscopy modeling, including [[Nonlinear optics|non-linear optical properties]] and core-level transitions. Krylov is also known for her development of efficient algorithms and software for quantum chemistry computations. She is one of the developers of the [[Open source|open-source]] libtensor<ref>{{cite web |title=epifanovsky / libtensor |url=https://github.com/epifanovsky/libtensor |website=github.com |publisher=[[GitHub]] |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=New implementation of high-level correlated methods using a general block-tensor library for high-performance electronic structure calculations.|journal=J. Comput. Chem.|volume=34|issue=26|pages=2293–2309|doi=10.1002/jcc.23377|pmid=24159628|year=2013|last1=Epifanovsky|first1=Evgeny|last2=Wormit|first2=Michael|last3=Kuś|first3=Tomasz|last4=Landau|first4=Arie|last5=Zuev|first5=Dmitry|last6=Khistyaev|first6=Kirill|last7=Manohar|first7=Prashant|last8=Kaliman|first8=Ilya|last9=Dreuw|first9=Andreas|last10=Krylov|first10=Anna I.|s2cid=5737454}}</ref> library for many-body calculations and the [[Q-Chem]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Q-CHEM Fast, Accurate, Robust Quantum Chemistry |url=https://www.q-chem.com/ |website=q-chem.com |publisher=[[Q-Chem]] |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref> electronic structure package.

Using the tools of [[computational chemistry]], and in collaboration with numerous experimental laboratories, Krylov also investigates the role that radicals and electronically excited species play in such diverse areas as combustion, gas- and condensed-phase chemistry, astrochemistry, solar energy, quantum information storage, bioimaging, and light-induced biological processes. She has authored over 300 publications and has delivered more than 300 invited lectures, including the 2012 Löwdin Lecture at [[Uppsala University]] in Sweden, the 2013 Coulson Lecture at the [[University of Georgia]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chem.uga.edu/seminars/categories/coulson-lecture/past|title=All Past Coulson Lectures - Department of Chemistry|website=www.chem.uga.edu|access-date=2 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180103072423/http://www.chem.uga.edu/seminars/categories/coulson-lecture/past|archive-date=3 January 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> the 2018 Davison Lecture at the [[University of North Texas]], and the 2023 [[Hans Hellmann]] Lecture at the [[Marburg University|Philipps-Universität Marburg]] in Germany.<ref>{{cite web |title=Verleihung der Hans-Hellmann-Lecture an Anna Krylov |url=https://www.uni-marburg.de/de/aktuelles/news/2023/hellmann-lecture2023-krylov |website=uni-marburg.de |publisher=[[Marburg University]] |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref>

=== Science education and outreach ===
Krylov has developed educational materials (computational labs<ref>{{cite web |title=Teaching with Q-Chem |url=https://www.q-chem.com/learn/ |website=q-chem.com |publisher=[[Q-Chem]] |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref> and tutorials)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Quantum Chemistry of Electronically Excited and Open Shell Species|url=https://winterschool.cc/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=3022:quantum-chemistry-of-electronically-excited-and-open-shell-species&catid=103|access-date=2021-08-15|website=Virtual Winter School on Computational Chemistry| date=20 January 2017 |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=From Orbitals to Observables and Back| date=6 December 2020 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y23CEnjlzts |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/y23CEnjlzts |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|language=en|access-date=2021-08-15}}{{cbignore}}</ref> aiming to increase quantum chemistry literacy among chemists. She has also developed films to help popularize science.  The two iOpenShell films, ''Shine a Light''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ceoO18RTiZI |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/ceoO18RTiZI |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|title=Shine a Light|date=4 August 2009|via=YouTube|access-date=2 January 2018}}{{cbignore}}</ref> and ''Laser'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fhiOQSc5n90 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/fhiOQSc5n90 |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|title=Laser|date=14 September 2009|via=YouTube|access-date=2 January 2018}}{{cbignore}}</ref> have been viewed more than 66,000 times on YouTube since September 2009. In 2015, Krylov delivered a public lecture in the [[Telluride, Colorado|Telluride]] Science and Innovation Center Town Talks series<ref>{{cite web |title=Town Talks |url=https://telluridescience.org/town-talks/ |website=telluridescience.org |publisher=Telluride Science and Innovation Center |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref> entitled “Molecules and Light: The Story of Life, Death, and our Quest for Knowledge”.

=== Awards ===
Krylov has received worldwide recognition, in particular for her invention of the spin-flip method.<ref name="auto" /><ref name="auto1" /> She received the 2007 [[WATOC]] (World Association of Theoretical and Computational Chemists) [[Dirac Medal (WATOC)|Dirac Medal]] for her "outstanding research on new methods in electronic structure theory for the description of bond-breaking, in particular the spin-flip method",<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ch.ic.ac.uk/watoc/|title=World Association of Theoretical and Computational Chemists|website=www.ch.ic.ac.uk|access-date=2 January 2018}}</ref> and the [[Agnes Fay Morgan Research Award]], given by [[Iota Sigma Pi]] [[National Honor Society]] for outstanding research achievements to a woman chemist or biochemist under 40 years of age. She is the recipient of a Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel Research Award from the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] for developing robust electronic structure methods for open-shell and electronically excited species and creative use of [[Ab initio quantum chemistry methods|''ab initio'' theory]] to understand the chemistry of biomolecules, reaction intermediates, and photoinduced processes; and the recipient of the 2012 Theoretical Chemistry Award from the Physical Chemistry Division of the [[American Chemical Society]].  In addition, she has received the USC Melon Mentoring Award, the Hanna Reisler Mentoring Award from the WiSE program, the USC Phi Kappa Phi Faculty Recognition Award, and the INSIGHT Into Diversity Inspiring Women in STEM Award.  In 2017, Krylov was recognized with the Mildred Dresselhaus Award from the Center for Ultrafast Imaging at [[DESY]] in Hamburg, Germany.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Maximal satisfaction comes from solving the hardest problems {{!}} CUI – The Hamburg Centre for Ultrafast Imaging|url=https://www.cui-archiv.uni-hamburg.de/en/2019/03/maximal-satisfaction-comes-from-solving-the-hardest-problems/index.html|access-date=2021-09-10|website=www.cui-archiv.uni-hamburg.de}}</ref> In 2018, she was awarded a Simons Fellowship in Theoretical Physics from the [[Simons Foundation]]. In 2020 she received the [[American Physical Society]]'s prestigious Earle K. Plyler Prize for Molecular Spectroscopy & Dynamics for her:<blockquote>"innovative work developing high accuracy electronic structure theory to inspire interpretation of spectroscopy of radicals, excited states, and ionization resonances in small molecules, biomolecules, and condensed phase solutes."<ref name=":2">{{cite web |title=APS award recipients {{!}} Anna Krylov, University of Southern California 2020 recipient, Earle K. Plyler Prize for Molecular Spectroscopy & Dynamics |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/winners?t=Earle%20K.%20Plyler%20Prize%20for%20Molecular%20Spectroscopy%20%26%20Dynamics&y=2020&af=false |website=aps.org |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref></blockquote>In 2022, she received the USC Associates Award for Creativity in Research and Scholarship,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Awards and Announcements 2022 > Department of Chemistry > USC Dana and David Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences |url=http://dornsife.usc.edu/chemistry/awards-announcements-2022 |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=dornsife.usc.edu |language=en}}</ref> the highest scholarly award granted by the University.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Associates Award for Creativity in Research and Scholarship – Office of Research Initiatives and Facilities |url=https://orif.usc.edu/funding/associates-award-for-creativity-in-research-and-scholarship/ |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=orif.usc.edu}}</ref> That same year, she received the inaugural Communicator of the Year Award, Science and Mathematics, from the USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts, and Sciences.  The award recognized her efforts to inform the scientific community and the general public through writings and speaking engagements of "the growing influence of politics and moral trends within STEM fields."<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Inaugural Communicator of the Year Awards honor scholars who engage with the public > News > USC Dornsife |url=http://dornsife.usc.edu/news/stories/3656/2021-communicator-of-the-year-awards/ |access-date=2022-03-28 |website=dornsife.usc.edu |date=21 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref> In 2023, Krylov was inducted into the American Academy of Sciences & Letters<ref>{{cite web |title=American Academy of Sciences & Letters |url=https://academysciencesletters.org/ |website=academysciencesletters.org |publisher=American Academy of Sciences & Letters |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref> and awarded the Academy's inaugural Barry Prize for Distinguished Intellectual Achievement.<ref>{{cite web |title=2023 Barry Prize for Distinguished Intellectual Achievement |url=https://academysciencesletters.org/awards/2023-barry-prize/ |website=academysciencesletters.org |publisher=American Academy of Sciences & Letters |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref>

Krylov is a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]],<ref name=":2" /> the [[American Chemical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=American Chemical Society names Fellows for 2015|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/pressroom/newsreleases/2015/july/acs-names-fellows-for-2015.html|access-date=2021-03-14|website=American Chemical Society|language=en}}</ref> the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]], and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=AAAS Members Elected as Fellows {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/aaas-members-elected-fellows-1|access-date=2021-03-14|website=www.aaas.org|language=en}}</ref>

=== Professional merit ===
Krylov has served on the editorial boards of numerous peer-review journals, including ''[[Annual Review of Physical Chemistry]]'', the ''[[The Journal of Chemical Physics|Journal of Chemical Physics]]'', the ''Journal of Physical Chemistry'', ''[[Chemical Physics Letters]]'', the ''[[International Journal of Quantum Chemistry]],'' ''[[Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics|Physical Chemistry–Chemical Physics]], [[Molecular Physics (journal)|Molecular Physics]],'' and ''[[WIREs Computational Molecular Science|Wires Computational Molecular Science]].'' She has served as a guest editor of special issues of [[The Journal of Physical Chemistry A|J''. Phys. Chem. A'']] honoring Prof. Benny Gerber<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=McCoy|first1=Anne B.|last2=Krylov|first2=Anna I.|last3=Buch|first3=Victoria|date=2009-07-02|title=Preface to the Robert Benny Gerber Festschrift|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/jp902677a|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry A|volume=113|issue=26|pages=7161–7162|doi=10.1021/jp902677a|bibcode=2009JPCA..113.7161M |issn=1089-5639|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and Prof. Hanna Reisler,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wittig|first1=Curt|last2=Sanov|first2=Andrei|last3=Reid|first3=Scott|last4=Krylov|first4=Anna|date=2019-08-01|title=Tribute to Hanna Reisler|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpca.9b04339|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry A|volume=123|issue=30|pages=6381–6383|doi=10.1021/acs.jpca.9b04339|pmid=31366202 |bibcode=2019JPCA..123.6381W |s2cid=199057047 |issn=1089-5639|url-access=subscription}}</ref> the special issue of ''Chemical Reviews on Theoretical Modeling of Excited-State Processes,''<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Matsika|first1=Spiridoula|last2=Krylov|first2=Anna I.|date=2018-08-08|title=Introduction: Theoretical Modeling of Excited State Processes|journal=Chemical Reviews|volume=118|issue=15|pages=6925–6926|doi=10.1021/acs.chemrev.8b00436|pmid=30086645 |issn=0009-2665|doi-access=free}}</ref> and the special issue of ''Physical Chemistry–Chemical Physics on Quantum Information Science.''<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Krylov|first1=Anna I.|last2=Doyle|first2=John|last3=Ni|first3=Kang-Kuen|author3-link=Kang-Kuen Ni|date=2021|title=Quantum computing and quantum information storage|url=http://xlink.rsc.org/?DOI=D1CP90024B|journal=Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics|language=en|volume=23|issue=11|pages=6341–6343|doi=10.1039/D1CP90024B|pmid=33704324 |bibcode=2021PCCP...23.6341K |osti=1777846 |s2cid=232194809 |issn=1463-9076}}</ref>  Currently, she is an associate editor of the journals ''Physical Chemistry-Chemical Physics'' ([[Royal Society of Chemistry]]) and ''Wires Computational Molecular Science'' ([[Wiley (publisher)|Wiley]]).

Krylov has organized numerous symposia and is a board member of [[WATOC]] and the International Society for Theoretical Chemical Physics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://istcp.org/|title=International Society for Theoretical Chemical Physics|website=ISTCP.org|access-date=2 January 2018}}</ref> She is the president of Q-Chem Inc.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://www.q-chem.com/|title=Quantum Computational Software; Molecular Modeling; Visualization|website=www.Q-Chem.com|access-date=2 January 2018}}</ref> and a developer of [[Q-Chem]], one of the world's leading [[Ab initio quantum chemistry methods|''ab initio'']] quantum chemistry programs. In addition, she is an elected member of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science|url=https://www.iaqms.org/members/krylov.php|access-date=2021-08-15|website=www.iaqms.org}}</ref> the [[Member of the Academia Europaea|Academia Europaea]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Academy of Europe: Krylov Anna|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Krylov_Anna|access-date=2021-07-15|website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref> and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2025 New Member List {{!}} American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/new-members-2025 |access-date=2025-04-23 |website=www.amacad.org |language=en}}</ref>

In addition to her permanent appointment at USC, Krylov is a Senior Professor by Special Appointment at Tel Aviv University. She has served as a visiting professor at [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]], [[University of Minnesota]] (Minneapolis), [[University of Colorado]] ([[JILA]]), [[Heidelberg University]], [[University of Mainz]], [[University of Groningen]], the Donostia International Physics Center<ref>{{cite web |title=Donostia International Physics Center (DIPC) |url=https://dipc.ehu.eus/en |website=dipc.ehu.eus |publisher=Donostia International Physics Center |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref> in Spain, and the Center of Ultrafast Imaging at [[DESY]] in Hamburg.

== Activism ==
Krylov is active in the promotion of gender equality in STEM fields, especially in theoretical chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Female chemists protest all-male conference lineup|url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2014/02/24/female-chemists-protest-all-male-conference-lineup|access-date=2021-09-10|website=www.insidehighered.com|language=en}}</ref> She created and maintains the web directory Women in Theoretical and Computational Chemistry, Material Science, and Biochemistry<ref>{{cite web|url=http://iopenshell.usc.edu/wtc/index.html|title=Women in theoretical/computational chemistry, material science, and biochemistry|website=iopenshell.USC.edu|access-date=2 January 2018}}</ref> that currently lists more than 400 scientists holding tenure and tenure track academic positions, or equivalent positions in industry, national laboratories, and other leading research establishments. She has delivered several talks on gender equality in STEM including a lecture at the international symposium in [[Uppsala]], Sweden.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://yacadeuro.org/women-in-science-2015/|title=Women in science 2015 – Young Academy of Europe|website=YAcadEuro.org|access-date=2 January 2018}}</ref>

Krylov is a founding member of the [[Academic Freedom Alliance]] and a member of its academic leadership committee.<ref>{{cite web |title=Leadership |url=https://academicfreedom.org/leadership/ |website=academicfreedom.org |publisher=[[Academic Freedom Alliance]] |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref> Her paper, "The Peril of Politicizing Science,"<ref>{{Cite journal|title=The Peril of Politicizing Science|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters|year=2021 |doi=10.1021/acs.jpclett.1c01475 |last1=Krylov |first1=Anna I. |volume=12 |issue=22 |pages=5371–5376 |pmid=34107688 |s2cid=235392946 |doi-access=free }}</ref> which "launched a national conversation among scientists and the general public"<ref name=":1" /> on the growing influence of political ideology over STEM, has received over 100,000 views and, according to [[Altmetric]], was the all-time highest-ranked article in the ''Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Altmetric – The Peril of Politicizing Science|url=https://acs.altmetric.com/details/107415981|access-date=2021-08-16|website=acs.altmetric.com}}</ref> Her works have been translated into [[Polish language|Polish]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Niebezpieczeństwo upolitycznienia nauki, Listy z naszego sadu |url=http://www.listyznaszegosadu.pl/nauka/niebezpieczenstwo-upolitycznienia-nauki |access-date=2024-01-26 |website=www.listyznaszegosadu.pl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Akademiccy ideolodzy korumpują STEM. Milcząca liberalna większość musi stawić opór, Listy z naszego sadu |url=http://www.listyznaszegosadu.pl/notatki/akademiccy-ideolodzy-korumpuja-stem-milczaca-liberalna-wiekszosc-musi-stawic-opalr |access-date=2024-01-26 |website=www.listyznaszegosadu.pl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sakowski |first=Łukasz |date=2023-08-16 |title=Nauka i ideologia kiedyś i dziś. Od ZSRR do Zachodu |url=https://www.totylkoteoria.pl/ideologizowanie-upolitycznianie-nauki-rosja-zachod/ |access-date=2024-01-26 |website=To Tylko Teoria |language=pl-PL}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title='Raniąca' idea merytorycznych podstaw nauki, Listy z naszego sadu |url=http://www.listyznaszegosadu.pl/raniacaa-idea-merytorycznych-podstaw-naukia |access-date=2024-01-26 |website=www.listyznaszegosadu.pl}}</ref> [[Estonian language|Estonian]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=AKADEEMIA nr. 4 – 2022 – pdf – AKADEEMIA |url=https://www.akad.ee/akadeemia-nr-4-2022-pdf/ |access-date=2024-01-26 |language=et}}</ref> French,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bons baisers de Russie : science et idéologie, hier en URSS et aujourd'hui aux États-Unis |url=https://factuel.media/blogs/blog-articles/bons-baisers-de-russie-science-et-ideologie-hier-en-urss-et-aujourdhui-aux-_ba_20539597 |access-date=2024-01-26 |website=factuel.media |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bons baisers de Russie : science et idéologie, hier en URSS et aujourd'hui aux États-Unis (Partie 2) |url=https://factuel.media/blogs/blog-articles/bons-baisers-de-russie-science-et-ideologie-hier-en-urss-et-aujourdhui-aux-_ba_20550577 |access-date=2024-01-26 |website=factuel.media |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bons baisers de Russie : science et idéologie, hier en URSS, aujourd'hui aux Etats-Unis (Partie 3) |url=https://factuel.media/blogs/blog-articles/bons-baisers-de-russie-science-et-ideologie-hier-en-urss-aujourdhui-aux-eta_ba_20551632 |access-date=2024-01-27 |website=factuel.media |language=fr}}</ref> and Russian.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vladimir |date=2023-12-12 |title=Опасность политизации науки |url=https://www.t-invariant.org/2023/12/opasnost-politizatsii-nauki/ |access-date=2024-01-27 |website=Т-инвариант / T-invariant |language=ru-RU}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Герчиков |first=Дмитрий |date=2024-02-12 |title=Страховка от "вредных знаний". Как работает цензура в научных публикациях |url=https://www.t-invariant.org/2024/02/strahovka-ot-vrednyh-znanij-kak-rabotaet-tsenzura-v-nauchnyh-publikatsiyah/ |access-date=2024-02-12 |website=Т-инвариант / T-invariant |language=ru-RU}}</ref>

In October 2025, Krylov declined to peer review a manuscript for [[Nature Communications]], cut ties with [[Nature Portfolio]], and published an open letter,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Krylov |first1=Anna|date=October 24, 2025 |title=Why I no longer engage with Nature publishing group |url=https://hxstem.substack.com/p/why-i-no-longer-engage-with-nature |website=hxstem.substack.com |publisher=Heterodox STEM via [[Substack]] |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref> and in November 2025, wrote an article,<ref name="article"/> calling for a [[boycott]] of [[Nature Portfolio#Journals|Nature journals]], accusing the publisher of abandoning its scientific mission in favor of a "social justice agenda". Among other criticisms, Krylov challenged [[Nature Reviews Psychology]] for encouraging "citation justice" practices aimed at "social-engineering their manuscript's bibliography to promote members of favoured identity groups", and [[Nature Human Behaviour]] for publishing what she termed a "censorship manifesto" declaring intent to censor research findings deemed potentially "harmful". The letter was endorsed by evolutionary biologist [[Richard Dawkins]]. [[Springer Nature]] representatives responded that citation diversity statements are optional for authors.<ref name="article">{{cite web |last1=Krylov |first1=Anna|date=November 12, 2025 |title=Why I Cut Ties with Science’s Top Publisher |url=https://www.thefp.com/p/why-i-cut-ties-with-sciences-top-publisher |website=thefp.com |publisher=[[The Free Press (Paramount Skydance)|The Free Press]] |access-date=13 November 2025}}</ref><ref name="Telegraph2025">{{cite news |last=Searles |first=Michael
 |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2025/10/26/top-journal-accused-science-over-social-justice-agenda/|title=Leading journal accused of abandoning science over 'social justice agenda'|newspaper=The Telegraph|date=2025-10-26|access-date=2025-10-27}}</ref>
